title: Where Does a Weight-Editing Agent Help? Blind Diagnosis and Repair of Deployment Faults in Vision Models
read_level: full (arXiv PDF v1 via pdftotext: Secs 1-11, Tables 1-9, Appendices A-C, E-F; per-run Table 11 in App. D only skimmed; Figures 1-3 as text)
why_wsp: A Claude Opus 5.5 agent reads a vision model's weights, runs budgeted forward passes (no gradients, no reference checkpoint), decides whether a deployment fault exists, diagnoses it, and submits an additive weight delta that inverts it; compared against forward-only scripts, test-time adaptation and fine-tuning.
facets: evaluation (agent vs script/TTA/fine-tune controls; pre-registered expectations; transcript audit)
domain: Vision model deployment/conversion faults: ImageNet classification, VOC segmentation, COCO detection
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (isolated sub-agents); diagnoses judged by Claude Code (second judge: Claude Opus 5.5 fresh context)
target: ResNet-50, ViT-B/16 (ImageNetV2), DeepLabV3-R50 (VOC 2012 val), Faster R-CNN R50-FPN (COCO val2017); plus a privately fine-tuned, channel-permuted DeepLabV3. Parameter counts not stated.
interface: code/tensor tools (agent reads state dict in Python, calls a forward tool returning predictions/activations, submits .npz additive delta; closed-form computations and offline combinatorial solvers allowed)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (up to 50 forward calls of <=200 images, 500 in classification; can test candidate deltas and see pool metric)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: null (not aggregated; edits are fault inverses on named tensors, e.g. first conv / BN running mean, flipped kernels, last-layer bias)

headline_results.quote: Over all rounds it repairs 123 of 162 faulted models, edits none of the 21 fault-free ones, and no edit lowers the score by more than 0.03 points

headline_results.claim: Post-hoc script matches agent on known families
headline_results.quote: a script written after the fact repairs 30 of 48 faults against the agent's 33
headline_results.where: Abstract; Sec 7.1, Table 7 ("30 of 48 faults against the agent's 33")

headline_results.quote: on five fault types outside every script it repairs 15 of 15 where that script repairs 4
With seven fault types on two models, 41 of 42 runs are repaired
Of the 24 faulted models 14 are repaired
With the reference 8 of 12 faulted models were repaired and none was missed; without it 4 of 12 were repaired and 4 were missed
Seven of 15 faulted models were repaired.
A correct diagnosis is followed by a repair in 115 of 124 runs, a wrong one in 0 of 13.
The agents repaired 8 of 9 faulted models ... all 12 diagnoses were correct, and the three fault-free models were not edited
without them 120 of 158 faulted models are repaired

cost.quote: the median number of forward calls was between 4 and 11 of the 50 allowed
We did not measure cost: an agent run takes minutes to an hour of model calls, a script seconds to minutes.

baselines_and_controls: Frozen forward-only script library (BN re-estimation, ridge refit / bias correction of last layer, best input channel order, input standardisation, class offset, outlier-row zeroing) and 'try-all' combination; entropy minimisation (Tent); last-layer and full fine-tuning on labelled pool; informed (ground-truth) edit as upper reference; post-hoc script LH written after seeing agent solutions; 21 fault-free models for false alarms; reference-statistics ablation on ViT; non-public fine-tuned+permuted checkpoint for memorization.
runs_and_variance: 183 agent runs; 3 seeds (instances) per condition, each run once; per-seed recoveries reported. Quote: "Each instance was run once and each condition has three instances, so the per-condition counts are descriptive" (Sec 10). No CIs.
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no post-edit fine-tuning/quantization); scored on locked test split of same deployment distribution
verification: Exact/near-exact informed inverse for every fault as ground truth; locked test split scored by authors; diagnoses judged against key by LM judge, second LM judge agreement "154 of 156 labels (Cohen's kappa = 0.97)" (Sec 7.3); rule audit of transcripts (App. E); pre-written expectations (App. F).
memorization_vs_reasoning: Repeated on a never-published fine-tuned checkpoint with random internal channel permutations: 8 of 9 repaired vs 9 of 9 on public; "This rules out that the diagnoses rest on remembered values or positions of the public file. It does not rule out general knowledge of how such networks look" (Sec 7.3). SCORECAL diagnosed from a training invariant (bias sum ~0) rather than reference copy.
limitations_stated: Single run per instance, 3 instances per condition; one agent model; synthetic, structured single/double faults (incl. 'unseen' types, chosen to lie outside the script); post-hoc script covers segmentation and detection only; excludes comparison with original model; non-public model derived from public; LM judges; isolation by rules+audit not technical barrier (6 runs flagged); detection-failure explanation not tested by intervention; cost not measured.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 (Sparks of WSP blog)
2611.21885 Fan et al., Language models can rewrite their own weights
Ropinski & Kranz 2026 (image classifier editing benchmark; no id given)
notes_for_survey: Evaluation-style WSP paper with non-agent controls fixed before agent runs: on known fault families a post-hoc script nearly matches the agent (30 vs 33 of 48), while on 5 fault types chosen to lie outside the script the agent repairs 15/15 vs 4/15 (authors note this test is one-sided). All 12 misses occurred where the model lacked a trustworthy per-layer activation reference (ViT without supplied stats; detector with frozen mismatched BN). Experiments, audit and diagnosis judging were run by an AI coding assistant (AI Use Statement).
